dimensions.note: No source change since 2026.10.27.1 apart from the version and its no-op upgrades entry (and deno.json excluding .review/ from fmt), so the finding of that review stands. The method tests sign with the fixtures' throwaway root pair given as values and assert, through assertNoSecret, that neither the root secret nor any FIXTURE-SECRET account secret reaches a record, a log or an error, on success and on a refused signature; the key file and transport tests keep their masking checks.

From that review: A backend without adminUrl is refused by the policy check; radosgw's listing-for-an-unknown-subresource is read as absent for ownershipControls, CORS and tags only, through one helper that rethrows anything else; JSON that is not JSON names what was expected.

65 unit tests pass. Every method (health, accounts, buckets, bucketSettings, inventory, check) runs through createModelTestContext with a stub fetch at the transport's __setFetch seam, a success and a failure path each, asserting on the records, their inventory tag, the requests made, and that a failed run writes nothing; check reads through a stubbed queryData and is asserted to ask only for its own inventory. The stub answers only listed routes and is reset with __setFetch() in a finally in every test. The parsers still read answers recorded from a throwaway gateway (the fixtures that remain); the deleted fixtures were only used by the old fake gateway. negative_test keeps the key-source, parser and check refusals. Fewer tests than the 90 of the last review; the backends and the lock rules are covered by findings_test and parse_test and live by smoke/. README's test paragraph matches.
